idea: Our own graded picks vs the market's closing fair odds, by tier and sport: is the model's win chance calibrated, and do leans/Locks beat the close?
data: data/ledger.json, 100 graded won/lost picks with a close_fair price (void picks dropped)
tuning: none (no parameters fitted; a calibration check)
blind: all picks are live, so every graded pick was unseen when posted
luck_control: 20,000 simulated seasons where each pick wins at the market's closing fair chance: leans (26 wins vs 32.8 expected) land that low or lower 5.7% of the time; Locks (2 of 7 vs 3.7) 17%; early picks (11 of 17 vs 8.5) high 17%
verdict: nothing proven, nothing to wire. Leans run 41% wins with the model saying 59% (market 51%), -23% ROI on 64 no-unit picks; the model's Brier score (0.272) is worse than the close's (0.257), so it is overconfident on leans and not better than the market. Early picks 11-6 (+25%) and the 5 dogs 4-1 are too few to trust. Units are only on proven types and the Lock's 0.5u, so little money rides on this. Watch: if leans stay below the close past ~150 graded, shrink lean win chances toward the market.
action: none; rerun weekly as the ledger grows

idea: Closing-line moves from the opener: dogs (+100 to +220) whose win chance rose 1/2/3+ points (steam toward the dog) or fell 1/2+ (drifting out), and favorites (-170 to -110) whose chance rose 2/3+ points
data: data/lines/espn/<sport> opening and closing moneylines (open lines 2023+, MLB 2019+)
luck_control: 100 random tenths of all +100..+220 dogs through the same bar: 0 of 100 passed; across 42 variants luck alone gives about 0.3 passes (1 in 150 each)
verdict: one variant passed the bar: NHL dog moved toward by 1%+ (tuning 223 bets +1.3%, blind 638 bets +8.5% +/-4.6%); 2% and 3%+ NHL dogs run +9% and +11% blind but lost in tuning (-5%, -15%) on 125 and 62 bets. Everything else lost or was flat: favorites that shortened lose in all six sports (MLB -7%, NCAAF -13% blind), dogs that drifted out lose, other sports' steam dogs flat. Not wired: the pass is one sport of 42, tuning is a single NHL season at +1.3%, and the live steam check uses first-seen price, not the true opener the study used.
action: none; keep watching NHL steam dogs. Code: sportsedge/movestudy.py (rerunnable, not in the daily run)

Not wired.
